summary: Summit lookout on Black Butte: station due for dedication 1931, wrecked in the 1962 storm, rebuilt 1963, moved off by 1975-77; only a concrete foundation remains.

facts.design: C-16 all-steel cabin (FFLOS); the replacement was specified on a concrete block base (clippings)
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest
facts.status_note: The cabin was moved off the summit; only a concrete foundation remains at the summit (Forest Service sheet).

access.note: Reached on foot by a trail from a trailhead off a gravel road.

visit.trail_note: About 2.56 miles from the trailhead to the summit, about 1,845 feet of climb, no water on the trail; the Forest Service maintains it each year.

events.note: Lookout station on the summit due for dedication October 1931; the trail to it dedicated that month (clippings). Building type not stated.
Lookout spotted a house fire in south Dunsmuir and raised the alarm; the house was destroyed.
Frank Jackson, Forest Service look-out on Black Butte (clipping dated October 22, 1943; again in a July 7, 1944 item).
Cecelia Thompson of Dunsmuir took the job; second season in 1962.
Columbus Day storm, October 1962. Sources differ on which building was lost.
Metal cabin rebuilt after the storm, materials lifted by helicopter; Mildred Weston moved in summer 1963.
Forest Service sheet: the lookout operated until 1973.
Forest Service sheet: the building was moved by helicopter to a new location.
FFLOS gives 1977 for removal, with relocation to Hogback Mountain that year.

corrections.proposed: 1931 built (lookout station on the summit); 1963 rebuilt after the October 1962 storm
corrections.why: Clippings and the Forest Service sheet describe a summit lookout from 1931 and a 1963 rebuild after the 1962 storm; the brief lists only the 1963 build.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 1977 for removal and relocation to Hogback Mountain; the Forest Service sheet says the building was moved by helicopter in 1975. The story reports both dates.
FFLOS calls the 1962 loss a Plan 4AR ground cabin blown off the mountain; the clippings say the original 1931 building blew away. The story reports both.
Clippings from 1931 describe a Forest Service trail to the lookout; the Forest Service sheet says the Civilian Conservation Corps built the trail in the late 1930s. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief records to check: height_m 4.0 is not supported by any page read here, so it is left out. The fflos_registered date (April 15, 2020) is not visible in the cached FFLOS text, so it is left out. The brief's coordinates (41.366537, -122.348119) differ from the west_us_lookouts point (41.39348, -122.36486); not resolved. Sources disagree on the 1975 vs 1977 move and on which 1962 structure was lost. The 1931 start comes from newspaper clippings only; no structure type is given for 1931. The FS sheet says the building was moved, so the 'today' paragraph describes only the foundation the sheet names.
